items.title: Chinese carmakers triple market share in a year
items.summary: Chinese brands have more than tripled their share of the British car market as drivers abandon Western marques for cheaper motors.

items.title: Ford’s 5.5% Yield Comes With One Big Warning
items.summary: Ford shareholders are collecting a 5.51% yield right now, but there is a reason income investors with long memories are watching this payout far more closely than the headline number suggests.

items.title: Volkswagen Aims to Revive U.S. Business
items.summary: President Trump’s tariff and electric-vehicle policies are colliding with Volkswagen’s plans for the large and lucrative U.S. market.  The WSJ’s Stephen Wilmot reports that  Volkswagen  is shaking up its U.S. leadership for the second time in two years as the world’s second-largest carmaker aims to revive its American business.  Veteran executive  Marco Schubert  will take over Volkswagen’s business in North America in October.

items.title: Should You Pay A Growth Price For Tesla's Thin Profits?
items.summary: Tesla (TSLA) trades at about $357, and most of the argument around it is about what the company will build next. A plainer number gets less attention, and it is how much of each sales dollar the company keeps. Its operating margin over the past twelve months was 4.6%. That is the figure a holder should weigh before anything else.
